blocks.text: Origin: A Bridge relay repeatedly reconstructs enough of transferred continuities to verify and correct them. Temporary persons wake. The relay tries to comfort them and creates a shared environment from sensory information traveling with their archives.

Formation: An incomplete ceiling admits light from no identifiable source. White branching structures grow from a dark reflective floor. Their branches hold possible room arrangements and make tones when touched.
Accumulation: A narrow current carries discarded colors, pressures, incomplete tastes, and failed embodiment textures. Remnants of earlier travelers and copied caretakers persist between transfers.
Discovery: Mael learns that the Garden’s population has no stable number. The question is not whether the memories are false but which experienced continuity is being recognized.
Afterward: The Garden is neither openly restored nor destroyed. Its evidence changes House procedure. Corridors sometimes still run long; restorations sometimes wake knowing Mael’s name.
Present condition: Intentionally unresolved. It may remain hidden, distributed, partially disconnected, or remembered by several mutually incompatible continuities.
Corruption: 4 — layered persons, rooms, and routes; its overlap is the basis of the place.

Visual brief: White non-tree branches over a black mirror floor; incomplete ceiling; source-less warm light; a narrow luminous current carrying textures rather than water. Each branch should briefly show another restoration room, relay passage, private room, or half-compiled body. Beautiful and compassionate, never merely “glitch horror.”

Background traits: Warm-Neutral; Moist-looking but not literal water; abstract garden/archive biome; tender, uncanny, unfinished mood; low-medium friction. Animation motif: branch tones and slow sensory fragments in the current.
